findings.pdf_says: Printed page 545 (PDF page 575) ends with '4) All instance objects are destroyed.' followed only by the footer. The block that begins 'NOTE  Any open files in an object are closed before the object is destroyed.' and runs through '14.6.13.1.1  General / An exception condition is either a condition associated with a specific exception status indicator or an exception object. ... specified in the RAISING phrase.' is printed EXACTLY ONCE, on printed page 546 (PDF page 576).
findings.markdown_says: specs/ISO_COBOL.md carries that entire page-576 body TWICE. First inside the page-575 slice at lines 24070-24108 (a stray '---', then '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', 'NOTE Any open files in an object are closed before the object is destroyed.', items 5)-7), '## 14.6.12 Abnormal run unit termination', ... '## 14.6.13.1.1 General', '... specified in the RAISING phrase.'), and again at lines 24110-24147 under ' / ## Page 576'.
findings.why_it_matters: About 40 lines of normative text for 14.6.11 items 5)-7), 14.6.12 and 14.6.13/14.6.13.1/14.6.13.1.1 are duplicated verbatim. The duplicate also re-emits the anchors '<a id="section-14-6-12">', '<a id="section-14-6-13">', '<a id="section-14-6-13-1">' and '<a id="section-14-6-13-1-1">', so every intra-document link to those sections resolves to the copy that has no page anchor and the wrong heading depths. Any grep-based citation workflow gets two hits for one rule and cannot tell which is canonical.
findings.suggested_repair: Delete specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 24069-24109 (the stray '---' at 24070 through the blank lines before '' at 24110), keeping the copy that begins at line 24110 - it is the one carrying the page anchor and the correct '### 14.6.13.1' / '#### 14.6.13.1.1' depths.

findings.pdf_says: Printed page 546 (PDF page 576) ends with '... in which the object is specified in the RAISING phrase.' and then the footer '546   ©ISO/IEC 2023'. Printed page 547 (PDF page 577) OPENS with the paragraph 'An exception status indicator is a conceptual entity that exists for each function, method, or program for each exception condition and has two states, set or cleared. findings.markdown_says: Line 24149, still inside the page-576 slice and BEFORE '' at line 24151: '546 �ISO/IEC 2023 An exception status indicator is a conceptual entity that exists for each function, method, or program for each exception condition and has two states, set or cleared. ...'. The page-577 slice then starts at its SECOND paragraph, 'In addition to exception status indicators, a last exception status exists for the entire run unit.'
findings.why_it_matters: The opening normative paragraph of 14.6.13.1.1 on page 577 - the definition of an exception status indicator, its two states, its initial cleared state and how TURN / PERFORM WHEN enable it - is attributed to the wrong page, so a page-cited lookup of page 577 misses it. The page-576 running footer has additionally been OCR'd into the body as literal text with a U+FFFD replacement character where '©' belongs, so the paragraph reads '546 �ISO/IEC 2023 An exception status indicator ...'.
findings.suggested_repair: Strip the inlined footer text '546 �ISO/IEC 2023 ' from line 24149 and move the remaining paragraph ('An exception status indicator is a conceptual entity ... to be executed.') to immediately after the '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' header line of the page-577 slice, ahead of 'In addition to exception status indicators, ...'.

findings.pdf_says: 14.6.13.1.4 item 3): '... If execution of the declarative completes normally, execution continues as specified in the statement for normal execution. If a conditional phrase with a NOT phrase is specified in the interrupted statement, the imperative-statement in that phrase is not executed.'
findings.markdown_says: '... If execution of the declarative completes normally, execution continues as specified in the rules for normal execution. If a conditional phrase with a NOT phrase is specified in the interrupted statement, the imperative-statement in that phrase is not executed.'
findings.why_it_matters: Altered wording in a normative general rule: the standard points at 'the statement' (the interrupted statement itself), the transcription at 'the rules'. The practical effect is the same, but the transcription is no longer quotable verbatim as ISO text, and rule 1 of this project requires citing the spec exactly.
findings.suggested_repair: In the page-580 slice, item 3) of 14.6.13.1.4, change 'as specified in the rules for normal execution' to 'as specified in the statement for normal execution'.

findings.pdf_says: Heading '14.6.2.4   Initial state of object data' - a fourth-level clause number, the same depth as 14.6.8.1 / 14.6.9.1, which the transcription renders at '###'.
findings.markdown_says: Line 23799: '## 14.6.2.4 Initial state of object data'
findings.why_it_matters: Heading depth is the transcription's only machine-readable encoding of clause nesting. At '##' this four-part clause sits at the same markdown level as its parent 14.6.2 and as three-part clauses like 14.6.3, so a generated table of contents or an outline fold shows it as a peer of its own parent.
findings.suggested_repair: Change line 23799 to '### 14.6.2.4 Initial state of object data' to match the file's dominant convention (three-part number -> '##', four-part -> '###', five-part -> '####').
